Title: Nursery teacher fined RM800 after pleading guilty to hurting autistic boy
Article:
KLANG: A nursery teacher was fined RM800 and sentenced to seven days' imprisonment in default after pleading guilty at the Magistrate's Court today to a charge of causing hurt to a seven-year-old autistic boy last month.
Magistrate Siti Zubaidah Mahat imposed the sentence on Lenah Abdul, 43, after taking into account the accused's guilty plea, as well as submissions from the prosecution and defence.
The mother of five was accused of intentionally causing hurt to the autistic child at approximately 10am on Aug 28, at a special education centre for children with special needs along Jalan Bendahara, Taman Sentosa.
The offence was alleged to have been committed when the accused was seriously and suddenly provoked, without any intention of causing hurt to any person.
She was charged under Section 334 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to one month, or a fine not exceeding RM1,000, or both, upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case, the complainant, the father of the autistic child, discovered bruises on the victim's left thigh, stomach, arm and cheek, believed to have been caused by hitting and pinching. He subsequently informed the boy's mother, who then contacted the nursery.
The nursery informed her that the victim had been uncontrollable on the day of the incident, causing the teacher on duty to lose her patience and strike the child using a clothes hanger. The victim's father then lodged a police report.
Earlier, the accused's lawyer, Adam Rosli, appealed for a lenient sentence on the grounds that his client has five school-going children, including one with autism who is registered as a person with disabilities.
He added that she earns only RM1,700 per month and has expressed remorse for her actions.
He submitted that the incident occurred while the accused was facing a difficult situation, as the victim was said to have repeatedly soiled his diaper and smeared faeces on the walls.
Additionally, on the day in question, he said that there were seven other active children under his client's care, which caused the situation to become unmanageable.
However, deputy public prosecutor Mohammad Uzzair Rosman urged the court to impose a commensurate sentence as a deterrent, considering that the accused was a teacher and caregiver entrusted with the responsibility of looking after the autistic child at the centre.
He submitted that the accused's failure to control her emotions had resulted in injuries to the victim, and that the offence involved a matter of public interest.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah welcomes feedback on Mount Kinabalu accessibility
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government welcomes constructive feedback on accessibility at Mount Kinabalu, but visitors should distinguish between facilities at Kinabalu Park and the physically demanding climb to the summit, said Datuk Jafry Ariffin.
Jafry, who is Sabah Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister said the summit route was naturally steep, rocky and physically demanding, making accessibility considerations different from those involving public facilities within Kinabalu Park.
"The summit route is naturally steep, rocky and physically demanding, making accessibility considerations different from those involving public facilities within Kinabalu Park," he said when contacted.
He was responding to comments on Google reviews about wheelchair accessibility and calls to "lower" the height of Mount Kinabalu.
Both reviews went viral on social media, prompting some netizens to question the practicality of the recommendations.
Jafry said Kinabalu Park offered visitors various experiences beyond summit climbing, including opportunities to appreciate its scenery, biodiversity and natural heritage.
"Kinabalu Park has been recognised as a Unesco World Heritage Site since 2000 and forms part of the Kinabalu Unesco Global Geopark.
"These prestigious international recognitions reflect its outstanding geological and biological significance.
"Our priority is to preserve its natural integrity while ensuring that the overall visitor experience remains safe, welcoming and as inclusive as reasonably possible," he said.
He said Sabah Parks would continue to assess and improve accessibility at appropriate public areas, subject to safety, terrain and conservation requirements.
Mount Kinabalu, standing at 4,095 metres,
hosted the 32nd International Climbathon
last year as part of the Skyrunning World Series.
Two years ago, the Sabah government launched Mount Kinabalu as the country's first
High-Altitude Training
Centre, involving climbs to four peaks above 3,900 metres.
Researchers have also found the world's largest pitcher plant species,
Nepenthes rajah,
and the Sumazau Orchid, scientifically known as Paphiopedilum rothschildianum, which is endemic to the Mount Kinabalu area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI could pose 'existential' risk to humanity, UN rights chief warns
Article:
GENEVA: UN rights chief Volker Turk warned on Monday that artificial intelligence could become powerful enough to threaten humanity, and said he would urge companies in the coming days to reduce the risks.
"I share the concerns of industry insiders that advanced AI could pose an existential risk to humanity," Turk told the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva in a sweeping speech ahead of the start of his second term next month.
"I am calling here, today, for an all-out effort to put cast iron guarantees in place around the safety and security of AI, before it is too late."
Without naming them, Turk warned that just a handful of men held "almost unlimited power over AI". Top AI companies include Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.
"At a minimum, we need countries hosting AI and those involved in its supply chains to come together around agreed red lines," he said.
Turk's remarks echoed prior warnings from top artificial intelligence executives themselves about extinction risks from AI, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.
The United Nations has called for harmonised rules to reduce the risks and held its first global meeting on governance in July.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Farmers forced to buy alternative fertiliser as Baja 3 delays persist
Article:
KANGAR: Delays in the distribution of additional compound fertiliser (Baja 3) have forced some padi farmers in Perlis to spend their own money on alternative supplies to save their crops.
Mohd Noor Hashim, 63, a farmer from Padang Besar Selatan, Kuala Perlis, said he has yet to receive the fertiliser as supplies only recently arrived at the Area Farmers Organisation (PPK) level.
He said only a few farmers have received the aid so far, while stock delivered to the PPK by the National Farmers Organisation (Nafas) remains at the initial stage of distribution.
"An estimated 78 per cent of farmers here have yet to receive it, even though the padi planted across my 2ha plot is now more than 70 days old," he said when contacted today.
To prevent severe losses, Mohd Noor had to purchase replacement fertiliser externally at RM70 per bag.
"I need eight bags, costing RM560. Previously, yield could reach five to six metric tonnes per hectare, but it is now expected to drop by up to 30 per cent due to this delayed fertilisation.
"My income is expected to shrink from RM10,000 per hectare to RM7,000. After four months of hard work in the fields, my income is now only around RM1,750 a month or RM58 a day," he said.
He said the current situation differs from previous seasons when all three types of fertiliser were ready before planting began, whereas now the crop is past two months old without any sign of fertiliser arriving.
In contrast, another farmer, Zamzuri Ishak, 42, managed to receive and apply the fertiliser earlier.
"I was fortunate because I received Baja 3 two months ago and applied it to my fields.
"However, other farmers are still waiting for their turn because the recent change in fertiliser distribution companies took some time," he said.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) confirmed it has opened an investigation paper into the delayed distribution of Baja 3 to farmers in the northern region.
It is understood that Kedah MACC received an official complaint from the Malaysian Paddy Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (Pesawah) on Aug 26 before initiating the probe.
The investigation focuses on complaints regarding supply delays by the company appointed by the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry to meet the needs of 100,000ha of padi cultivation under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada).
The comprehensive probe by MACC will examine not only potential criminal and corruption elements, but also governance weaknesses at any management level that led to the critical delay.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian Sikh aid team reaches remote Nepal base after 16-hour journey
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A five-member team from United Sikhs Malaysia has reached Dhunche in Nepal's Rasuwa district, near the Nepal-Tibet border, where it will establish a base camp for a humanitarian mission.
According to a Facebook update, the team arrived at 11.14pm local time (approximately 1.30am Malaysian time) today, following a 16-hour drive from Kathmandu.
Footage showed the team navigating rocky, untarred roads through pitch-black darkness, with no lampposts, and at one point becoming stuck near a roadside bridge.
"We have been travelling from 7am and now we have been travelling for approximately 16 hours," a volunteer said in the video.
Yesterday, the team met the Smart team and Wisma Putra officials in Kathmandu to
coordinate flood relief efforts
before heading to Dhunche to unload relief supplies.
From there, it is expected to continue off-road to Syapru Besi, about 40km from the Nepal-Tibet border.
The team is expected to stay for two weeks, reaching underserved and hard-to-access areas to distribute essential supplies and temporary shelter materials to about 300 affected families.
Today, Nepal observed a national day of mourning, 13 days after the Rasuwa flash floods killed more than 1,355 people.
Seventeen Malaysians
remain uncontactable
in Rasuwa, while 5,500 people remain missing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt eyes greater pay transparency: Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Economy Ministry is exploring mechanisms to make salary offers more transparent, giving young workers greater room to compare pay and negotiate with employers, said its minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
The ministry is also assessing the need to raise the share of employee compensation in the economy, to ensure workers' returns improve in tandem with the country's economic growth.
The issue is particularly pertinent given Malaysia's median wage of around RM3,600, with Bumiputera workers continuing to record lower median incomes.
"It is not about having one absolute figure, but more about openness and transparency in terms of the salaries being offered.
"So, we need to look at the mechanisms that can be introduced," Akmal said after the Bumiputera Economy Plan Transformation forum today.
"This is something I have not discussed yet. This is the result of today's forum, which I will bring to the ministry for us to examine how we can elevate wages."
Akmal said the government's role should go beyond existing measures such as the minimum wage and progressive wage policy.
He said the government should also consider how workers could have a stronger voice in determining their remuneration, particularly young people and those entering the workforce.
He added that the lack of transparency could weaken workers' bargaining power, particularly during job interviews, where they had little basis to negotiate without a clear salary range.
"When we talk about salary, usually workers are only represented by unions that look at the current situation. But particularly among young people and those seeking jobs, where is their voice?
"For me, the first issue for us to move further on the salary issue is how this can be more open. Because this is the complaint of young people," he said.
Akmal said young workers often faced salary offers on a "take it or leave it" basis, making it difficult for them to compare opportunities and determine whether the remuneration offered was fair.
Akmal said the increase in the minimum wage to RM1,700 currently represented a significant rise compared with the rate when it was first introduced about a decade ago.
However, the discussions on wage structures and increases must continue periodically.
He said the effort was important to ensure graduates have pathways to jobs offering higher incomes, including through greater participation in high-income industries.
This, he cited the semiconductor sector, saying reports received by him showed some fresh graduates could start at about RM5,000 to RM5,500 monthly after completing relevant training programmes.
However, he said moving into higher-value industries required stronger foundations in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM).
"I see perhaps some quick wins that we can look at together, particularly how we can ensure Bumiputera children can compete healthily outside and that there is openness, so they know the salaries they receive are based on merit."
This would not only improve workers' earnings, but also support the career development the country aspires to achieve.
"We can further strengthen these efforts to ensure workers receive better returns.
"Ultimately, if we increase the share going to workers, the productivity they deliver must also increase correspondingly, in line with their wages," Akmal added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tokyo's Shinjuku to ban more than half of holiday rentals
Article:
TOKYO: Tokyo tourist hotspot Shinjuku will impose a ban on more than half of its holiday rentals, including homes on Airbnb, after a surge in complaints about visitors, an official said Monday.
Known for its buzzing commercial and entertainment district, Shinjuku has around 4,000 short-term rentals, according to the ward's official website. That is nearly 10 per cent of Japan's total.
But its large residential population has become increasingly exasperated with tourists who fail to properly dispose of rubbish, smoke where they are not supposed to and make too much noise.
A Shinjuku official supervising holiday rentals told AFP that the district was "planning to revise the current ordinance... to ban private lodging" in residential zones and areas near schools.
"As the number of private lodging businesses has risen, complaints and troubles around them have increased," the official said on customary condition of anonymity.
More than 50 per cent of short-term rentals in Shinjuku face a ban under the new rules, he said, adding that the plan would formally be announced by the Shinjuku mayor on Tuesday.
The policy will only apply to existing rentals, the official said. It is likely to result in the closure of around 2,000 properties, including an unknown number on Airbnb.
Japan aims to attract 60 million foreign tourists by 2030, up from 42 million in 2025, but overtourism has emerged as a major challenge.
Residents of Japan's former imperial capital Kyoto and other hotspots have expressed annoyance at selfie-taking crowds, as well as traffic congestion and soaring land prices.
In Shinjuku, the number of complaints over holiday rentals increased by around 40 per cent in the fiscal year to March, the official said.
[[nid:1527654]]
"Many complaints are about the violation of rubbish disposal rules while others include smoking and trespassing," he said.
American tourist Luke Jemison, 24, told AFP that the rules "make sense, because of noise."
Masaru Sato, a Shinjuku resident in his 70s, said "many foreigners, including operators of private lodgings, don't follow local rules."
"This area gets dirty because the way they dispose of rubbish is very messy," he told AFP.
AFP has contacted Airbnb for comment. Several hosts in Shinjuku declined interviews when contacted by AFP.
In July, the Japan Tourism Agency gave municipalities the right to regulate short-term lodgings if "a tranquil living and educational environment" is under threat or if they "hinder the maintenance of a permanent population and local community."
Kyoto is also considering a ban on short-term lodging, but only for new rentals within residential and industrial areas.
Other global cities have cracked down on private lodgings available through online rental platforms.
That is partly due to overtourism concerns, but also because some residents say home-sharing websites for tourists deprive locals of apartments for long-term rent and push up prices for homes remaining on the market.
Barcelona, one of Europe's most-visited cities, aims to ban apartment rentals to tourists by 2029 to ease a housing shortage.
Under rules introduced in 2023, New York prohibits rental periods of less than 30 days unless the host lives in the property.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tech pilgrims flock to China as global innovation race heats up
Article:
HUMANOID robots working on factory floors, AI models challenging global rivals and electric-vehicle plants churning out cars at breathtaking scale are drawing a new wave of foreign visitors to China.
Investors and entrepreneurs are paying thousands of dollars for rare access to Chinese factories, seeking a front-row seat to what many believe could be the next technological revolution.
The influx reflects mounting fears of a "China shock 2.0", with Western boardrooms and capitals confronting the possibility that Chinese companies are seizing the lead in advanced manufacturing and cutting-edge technologies.
"Right now, people are looking at China as an object of study and learning — a trend that barely existed just a few years ago," says Robert Wu, CEO of Shanghai-based data research firm Baiguan.
He noted that visitors often arrive with misconceptions — for instance, assuming China's robotaxi sector leads the US, when domestic policy caution around potential job losses actually keeps it a step behind.
Wu has organised two tours for more than two dozen investors, entrepreneurs and executives so far, charging up to US$15,000 for a five-day programme.
Around half the participants came from Southeast Asia.
He is part of a growing cottage industry catering to foreign demand for first-hand access to China's innovation ecosystem.
Many attendees avoid publicising their visits. Among those known to have made the trip are US investment firms Dimension, Capital Group and Thrive Capital, as well as US tech podcaster Lex Fridman.
While data on tech tours is scarce, broader industrial tourism is booming. China's industrial tourism sector pulled in US$17.8 billion last year, according to state media, and is projected to blow past 300 billion yuan (US$44.6 billion) by 2029.
Shanghai-based tech tour agency Glopen says inquiries jumped 50 per cent in 2026 from mostly European and Singaporean clients, and it now runs over 100 single-day company tours every month.
"You cannot grasp the true scale, speed, and physicality of Chinese innovation without standing on the factory floor," says Bertrand Chen, CEO of the Global Shipping Business Network, who joined an April three-city robotics and emerging tech tour organised by Chinese American investor Rui Ma.
Ma, founder of Tech Buzz China and organizer of 11 such tours since 2019, frames it as essential due diligence:
"Even if you're not actively investing in China, you're increasingly likely to encounter Chinese companies as competitors, partners, suppliers, or investments in markets around the world."
[[nid:1527648]]
The circuit spans Beijing, Shenzhen, Shanghai, Hangzhou and Hefei, the industrial powerhouses at the heart of China's electric-vehicle, battery, AI and robotics boom.
World leaders have also flocked to Xiaomi's Beijing auto factory, while Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz was famously filmed watching Unitree's dancing humanoid robots in Hangzhou, a high-profile showcase of the country's technological ascent.
None of this is happening by accident.
Beijing has explicitly pledged to "vigorously promote" industrial tourism, designating over 140 official demonstration sites. A growing number of factories are offering public tours at around US$60 a pop.
Xiaomi's EV factory has welcomed more than 250,000 visitors since March 2024. Demand is so intense that lottery-awarded entry slots are scalped online for up to 2,000 yuan (US$300).
For European executives wrestling with sluggish productivity growth and fears of falling behind in AI and robotics, China has become a particularly important destination.
Alex Shengyun Lu, a Shanghai-based AI consultant at Praxis Advisory, has led seven delegations of up to 50 corporate visitors since late 2025 and describes an uneasy mood.
"The smartest people in Europe are acutely aware of the situation. The insecurity is palpable," he says.
Executives typically arrive seeking answers to two questions, Lu said: what they can learn from Chinese companies and from China's state-backed approach to technology investment.
"They are coming here with a genuine mindset of humility and learning."
No city embodies the trend more than Shenzhen. Taxis now carry English-language announcements and foreign influencers regularly appear at tech exhibitions.
Czech entrepreneur Jan Smejkal, who has lived in the city for 11 years, says scarcely a day passes without a request from foreign startup founders keen to visit.
"There is no other place on earth that takes technology to its core and integrates it into daily life quite like Shenzhen."
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11-year-old Penang pupil strikes gold in UK public speaking contest
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Eleven-year-old Nur Aamily Saffiya Muhd Zabari Izyan has made her mark on the international stage by winning gold in a public speaking contest at the University of Surrey in the United Kingdom.
The SK Permatang Tok Mahat pupil also finished among the top three overall participants in the English category at the competition last month.
In February, Aamily won a silver medal in a public speaking competition in Dubai.
Education Minister and Nibong Tebal member of parliament Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said Aamily's achievements highlighted the importance of building confidence and encouraging children to embrace new opportunities.
"I like seeing children like this. It is not merely about the medals they bring home, but because at 11, her world is already so wide to explore," she said in a Facebook post.
Fadhlina said she recently met Aamily and her family and presented the pupil with an iPad to support her learning and encourage her to explore new areas of knowledge.
"As education minister, this is the confidence we want to cultivate in our children — to dare to try, dare to speak and dare to enter new spaces," she added.
Fadhlina said she was particularly proud of Aamily's achievement as she was a pupil from her constituency.
"This is our child. Continue to soar high, Aamily," she said.

Title: Police arrest man for locking wife and four children inside home
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Police have arrested a 36-year-old man for assault and unlawful confinement after he allegedly locked his wife and four children inside their home in Desa Mutiara, Jalan Gong Badak.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said police acted after receiving an emergency call from the victim, who reported that she was being abused and locked inside the house by her husband.
A team from the Gong Badak police station rushed to the scene following the call.
"Upon arrival, police found the woman inside the house with her four children, with all the doors secured with padlocks.
"After officers identified themselves, the victim said she had been beaten by her husband and locked inside.
"She requested police assistance to unlock the doors, prompting officers to cut the padlocks to free them," he said.
Azli said this when met after the Kuala Terengganu district police headquarters Merdeka Kayak Expedition at Pulau Warisan today.
He said a physical examination revealed injuries to the victim's right eye, along with pain in her head and left knee.
"The woman and her four children were brought to the police station for further action. Initial investigations suggest the suspect attacked the victim out of jealousy.
"Police then asked the suspect to surrender to assist in the investigation. The 36-year-old man arrived at the Gong Badak police station at 3pm yesterday before being arrested.
"A background check revealed the suspect has three prior criminal and drug-related offences, and initial questioning showed he admitted involvement in the case being investigated," he said.
Azli added that the suspect has been remanded for four days starting today to facilitate investigations under Sections 324 and 326A of the Penal Code.

Title: Japanese sushi chain ends Chiikawa rollout after staff caught selling freebies online
Article:
TOKYO: A Japanese sushi chain was forced to cancel a popular marketing campaign with goods featuring cute hamster-like characters from the hit franchise "Chiikawa" after its staff stole the freebies to resell online.
Conveyor-belt chain Kura Sushi launched its Chiikawa campaign on August 21 with plans to distribute a limited number of branded items like pouches and plates on a first-come-first-served basis through the end of September.
It also offered customers a chance to win key chains, magnets and other trinkets by trading in empty sushi plates for a turn at a prize-yielding game machine.
Earlier this month, Kura Sushi spokesperson Hiroyuki Kosaka told Reuters that virtually every table at its restaurants offering the Chiikawa giveaways had been booked for the rest of the month.
But on Sunday, the company abruptly ended the campaign after it confirmed what many fans had suspected: that store staff had stolen the goods and sold them online.
Since then, Kura Sushi's stores have been inundated with calls to cancel reservations, Kosaka said.
"We are truly sorry for causing the trouble and disappointing customers," he said.
Kura Sushi's shares closed down 2.5 per cent at 1,696 yen on Monday in Tokyo, compared with a 0.55 per cent rise for the broader TOPIX index.
The marketing debacle is the latest example of how corporate collaborations with popular franchises can go awry.
Last year, McDonald's Japan sparked controversy after separate tie-ups with Chiikawa and Pokemon prompted many customers to buy large quantities of Happy Meals to get the free toys to resell, while disposing of the food.
Created in 2020, Chiikawa — a truncated version of the Japanese phrase meaning "something kind of small and cute" — has risen to a level of dizzying popularity to become one of Asia's most sought-after licensing properties; its partners include Japanese airline ANA, Fast Retailing's Uniqlo and Hong Kong jeweller Chow Tai Fook, which offers a collection of gold Chiikawa accessories.
Belying their cuddly appearance, Chiikawa characters live stressful lives filled with trials and tribulations: searching for work as day labourers, struggling with exams and stressing over salaries, to name a few.
The jarring disconnect between their looks and grim predicaments has attracted a wide range of fans, including men, women and children.
Its maiden film released this year, "Chiikawa: The Secret of the Mermaid Island," grossed 12.2 billion yen (US$78 million) in Japan in just over a month, according to entertainment news website Mantanweb, further boosting the franchise's popularity.
Chiikawa's X account has 5.4 million followers, among them Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama.
When Kura Sushi teamed up with Chiikawa for a second time in March 2024, same-store sales jumped 23 per cent from a year earlier. Customer response this time around went beyond expectations, spokesperson Kosaka said.
The company said it continued to investigate the theft but declined to elaborate.
The Chiikawa freebies have become collectables fetching lofty prices.
Mercari, Japan's biggest online, second-hand market, had listings for a set of four Chiikawa-Kura Sushi cups and plates for 13,333 yen (US$85.54) and a set of three cups for 9,500 yen.
Kura Sushi said it had successfully asked Mercari to remove the collaboration items that were obtained illegitimately from its site.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EU still buying Russian LNG - Russian deputy foreign minister
Article:
VLADIVOSTOK: Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) is still being supplied to the European Union, but the volumes are incomparably smaller than in the past, Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Grushko told RIA Novosti.
Financial Times previously reported citing analysts that the EU had purchased nearly 10 million tonnes of gas from the Yamal LNG project from January to June 2026.
According to the newspaper, this is 18 per cent more than in the same period last year.
"As for the overall picture, our LNG is indeed flowing," Grushko said on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum.
He also noted that gas supplies to the EU today were incomparably smaller than previous records, when Russia's share of the EU's gas balance was approximately 40 per cent.
The EU Council previously approved a regulation phasing out imports of Russian LNG and pipeline gas.
The ban on LNG imports under short-term contracts came into effect on April 25, and on long-term contracts on January 1, next year.
The ban on pipeline gas began on June 17, for short-term contracts, and on November 1, next year, for long-term contracts.
The Eastern Economic Forum was held from September 1 to 4 in Vladivostok. RIA Novosti is the general media partner of the EEF. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zara would have remained in coma if she survived, inquest told
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A doctor told the father of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir that his daughter would have remained in a coma for the rest of her life had she survived her critical injuries, the Coroner's Court heard today.
The 80th witness, Mahathir Mohd Hashim @ Marikin, 45, said the doctor also told him that Zara had suffered serious injuries, including bleeding in the brain, lungs and kidneys, as well as a broken leg.
"I was informed by the doctor that Zara's condition was critical. She told me that if Zara survived, she would remain in a coma for the rest of her life.
"She also informed me that Zara had suffered serious injuries involving bleeding in the brain, lungs and kidneys, as well as a broken leg," he said while reading his witness statement before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
Mahathir said a doctor confirmed Zara's death at Queen Elizabeth Hospital (HQE) on July 17, 2025, while he was with the doctor.
He said he was never asked whether he consented to or objected to a post-mortem being carried out on his daughter.
Mahathir said he had remained at HQE from July 16 to 17, sleeping within the hospital grounds while waiting for news on Zara.
He arrived at the emergency unit between 1pm and 3pm on July 16 after learning that his daughter had been admitted.
He said he saw Zara's mother outside the emergency unit and, after being directed to her daughter's location, obtained permission from a nurse to visit Zara at her bedside.
Mahathir said he saw two female doctors, wearing dark blue uniforms, attending to Zara. He could not recall their names or positions.
While at Zara's bedside, he noticed that the pillow under her head was covered in blood.
"After that, I held Zara's head and kissed her forehead.
"When I held the back of Zara's head, I could feel that the area at the back of her upper neck was soft and seemed to have an indentation. I also noticed her left leg was bandaged from the thigh down to the sole of her foot," he said.
Mahathir also said he met several female teachers outside the emergency unit and asked what had happened to Zara and whether they were female wardens.
However, they introduced themselves as History and Bahasa Melayu teachers.
Zara, 13, was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school dormitory on July 16, 2025, and was pronounced dead at HQE the following day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal marks national mourning day after deadly flood
Article:
KATHMANDU: Grief-stricken Nepalis entered the traditional Hindu last day of mourning on Monday for the hundreds who died in the catastrophic flood along the country's border with China even as the government kept search operations going after four miracle rescues in recent days.
Government offices in the Hindu majority nation of 30 million people and at missions abroad would fly the national flag at half-mast to mark the 13th day after death, the home ministry said in a statement.
The day is considered the final day of mourning by the faithful, who commemorate it with rituals and food offerings.
A huge wall of mud and rock, triggered by a glacier breaking off, collapsed into a river on the Himalayan border of Nepal and China's Tibet on Aug 26, washing away towns and villages and burying roads and highways under piles of mud and debris.
At least 1,380 people have been killed by the mudslide and more than 5,500 are missing.
In recent days, search teams in Nepal have rescued four people, including a Chinese national who was pulled from a tunnel on Saturday.
The others were two hydropower workers rescued from another tunnel on Friday and a Nepali woman pulled out from her buried house on Saturday.
[[nid:1527613]]
Rescue operations in Nepal were focused on hydropower stations in the region, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said, where authorities believe there might still be survivors.
Chinese officials said on Sunday that workers had recovered 12 more bodies as the search continued for hundreds still missing in Tibet.
With search teams still looking for survivors, the government has not planned any wider events for the final day of mourning.
"There are no government programmes organised as the rescue and search operation is still going on in the flood-hit areas," Phanindra Paudel of the National Emergency Operation Centre (NEOC) told Reuters.
President Ram Chandra Paudel, the ceremonial head of state, was touring flood-hit areas on Monday and would survey damage caused by the disaster, his aide said.
Security personnel at the district jail in Nuwakot, one of the two worst affected districts, saved 923 prisoners by shifting them to a building in a higher location before flood waters entered their low-lying building, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a social media post.
Authorities also captured 50 prisoners who had broken the prison wall and gates as flooding began, and had fled barely 100 metres, Shah said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Toddler mauled by 5 stray dogs stable after surgery
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 2-year-old girl who was critically injured after she was believed to have been attacked by five stray dogs on Saturday is stable after undergoing surgery yesterday.
A family member, who wished to be known only as Nur, 23, said the operation at Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Baru went smoothly.
"The operation went smoothly, and I was told that doctors are monitoring her condition. She is now stable.
"I hope she recovers soon," she said when met today.
Nur recounted the harrowing moments when she rescued the girl, Nur Haira Watikah Mohammad Hamizi, during the attack at about 7am.
"I can still picture her face. She was extremely weak and breathing very slowly. I carried her while her body was covered in blood.
"It was heartbreaking to see her lying there with her eyes open. She appeared to be in great pain.
"She had lost so much blood that it soaked my clothes. I was too stunned to speak.
"I was inside the house when my mother screamed. I rushed outside to save her while my mother chased the dogs away," she said.
Nur said the attack had brought home the family's longstanding fears over the presence of stray dogs in the area.
"We have been worried about these stray dogs for a long time, but this time, it happened to someone in our family.
"Even adults are afraid of dogs, let alone children. It may not happen to us, but it could happen to someone else," she said.
Haira
was found lying
in front of her grandmother's house with severe wounds to her head and face following the attack.
Her parents had sent her to stay with her grandmother, Darlinda Darlis, 56, during the school holidays. Her elder brother was also staying at the house.
The police are investigating the case under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 for child neglect and Section 289 of the Penal Code for negligence involving an animal.
An offence under Section 31(1)(a) carries a maximum fine of RM50,000, imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both.
Section 289 provides for imprisonment of up to 6 months, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar to chair MA63 implementation action council meeting in Sabah this Friday
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to chair the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting at the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) here this Friday (Sept 11).
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor are also expected to attend, with Sabah hosting the meeting.
"For everyone's information, the MA63 Implementation Action Council meeting will be held this Friday, Sept 11, chaired by the Prime Minister and attended by the Sarawak Premier, with our Chief Minister hosting the meeting.
"There will also be a special MA63 session. I will address the relevant matters then," he said when asked to comment further on MA63-related issues at a contribution presentation ceremony for fire victims at Kolej Tingkatan Enam Prauniversiti Kota Kinabalu today.
Mustapha said the meeting is one of the main platforms for discussing matters related to the implementation of MA63 between the federal government, Sabah and Sarawak.
The MA63 Implementation Action Council meeting is among the key mechanisms for discussing and coordinating matters concerning the rights and interests of Sabah and Sarawak under the agreement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Delhi court order seen as limited impact on IHH Healthcare
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Delhi High Court's order concerning IHH Healthcare Bhd's investment in India's Fortis Healthcare Ltd is not expected to have any material impact on the group's strategic plans or operations, analysts said.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said Fortis and IHH Healthcare remain confident that the company is compliant with applicable laws.
Importantly, HLIB said no changes to Fortis' or IHH Healthcare's strategic plans are expected, while patient volumes and doctor flows remain unaffected.
"No material changes are expected.
"Fortis will continue to pursue its brownfield expansion and merger and acquisition (M&A) strategy, while IHH remains focused on increasing its stake in Fortis to 51 per cent from 31.17 per cent and integrating Gleneagles India with Fortis," it said.
HLIB said IHH Healthcare's patient visits have remained unaffected, as patients continue to focus primarily on the quality of healthcare services rather than the group's corporate structure or ongoing legal matters.
Similarly, it noted that doctors remain attracted to the Fortis brand and the clinical complexity of its operations, supported by the existing leadership.
"Investors should focus on the recent positive earnings surprise and stronger earnings momentum expected across regions in the second half of financial year 2026.
"Notably, Fortis' share price has not experienced material de-rating following the Delhi High Court's 31 Aug order, suggesting that investor concerns have remained relatively contained."
HLIB reiterated its "Buy" call on IHH Healthcare with an unchanged target price RM9.10.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has maintained its view that the ongoing legal proceedings will not have any material impact on Fortis' operations.
The firm said this is particularly given IHH Healthcare's arm's-length acquisition process and the absence of any evidence suggesting direct dealings with the Singh brothers.
"IHH Healthcare also reaffirmed its commitment to gradually increasing its stake in Fortis to 51 per cent over the next four years, and we expect this to have minimal impact on our target price."
CIMB Securities kept its "Buy" call and target price of RM10.30, and made no changes to our financial years 2026 to 2028 earning per share estimates.
Meanwhile, RHB Research highlighted that the court order is purely an investigative fact-finding exercise and contains no new evidence directly implicating IHH Healthcare or imposing monetary liability on it and Fortis.
While a temporary trading overhang, the firm said environmental, social and governance score pressure, or regulatory scrutiny from Securities and Exchange Board of India could linger during the audit period.
"Any resulting share price weakness is an attractive entry point, since fundamental growth drivers remain intact," it said.
Following a joint briefing held by IHH Healthcare and Fortis, RHB Research has affirmed its positive stance on the stock, as it views the company's fundamental growth drivers.
The firm reiterated its "Buy" call with an unchanged target price of RM9.54.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court urged to settle constitutional question before Undangs' contempt proceedings
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal should determine whether the Special Court has exclusive jurisdiction over a ruling chief before committal proceedings against six Negri Sembilan Undangs at the Seremban High Court can proceed, a lawyer said today.
Awang Armadajaya Awang Mahmud, who represents the appellants, said the issue arose from the interpretation of Articles 182 and 183 of the Federal Constitution, which govern the jurisdiction of the Special Court.
He said the key question was whether the term "Ruler" under Article 182 included a ruling chief and, if so, whether the Special Court had exclusive jurisdiction over proceedings involving a ruling chief.
"This is a serious and big question of law. When the High Court allowed the injunction and then gave permission for committal proceedings to proceed, the question arises as to whether the High Court had encroached on the jurisdiction of the Special Court.
"The appellants should be given the opportunity to present their full appeal so that this question of law can be answered," he said.
Awang Armadajaya said Article 182(3) expressly provided that the Special Court had exclusive jurisdiction to try specified offences committed in the Federation by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong or a Ruler of a state, as well as certain civil proceedings involving them.
He submitted that the constitutional issue had become particularly significant after the High Court granted an injunction and gave leave to the appellants to commence committal proceedings against the appellants.
Awang Armadajaya, who appeared with Datuk Mohammed Rhiza Ghazi and Choo Shi Jin, was seeking a stay of committal proceedings against his appellants, who are alleged to have breached an ad-interim injunction issued by the High Court on June 5.
The six appellants are former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Undang Luak Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri and Shahbandar Sungai Ujong Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid.
Previously, the Seremban High Court granted the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negri Sembilan (DKU) and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, leave to commence committal proceedings against the six for contempt of court, arising from the alleged breach of the injunction order.
On July 8, all six filed appeals against the decision of High Court judge Roz Mawar Rozain, who ruled that there was a prima facie case against them and ordered them to answer the committal application.
Roz Mawar also dismissed their application for a stay of committal proceedings pending the disposal of their appeal.
Meanwhile, lawyer Steven Thiru, representing DKU and Raja Norazli, said the committal proceedings at the High Court should be allowed to proceed without delay.
"This is in accordance with the settled principle that once contempt proceedings have been commenced, these proceedings should be given priority over all other proceedings," he said, adding that there were no exceptional circumstances to grant a stay.
He said the appellants sought the stay as a form of protection against committal proceedings which stemmed from their own disobedience of a court order.
"They have failed to demonstrate any sufficient basis for the court's discretion in their favour and we pray that their appeal is dismissed with costs," he said.
After a short deliberation, a 3-member appellate bench chaired by judge Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, sitting with Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Amarjeet Singh Serjit Singh, unanimously set Sept 14 for case management via e-review to set a decision date.
The judges also allowed the ad-interim stay issued by another appellate panel on July 29 to be extended until the decision.
Thiru was assisted by David Dinesh Mathew, Gregory Das, Shafrin Halim and Gurjeevan Singh Sachdev.
Also on Awang's team were Asmawi Ismail and Emirul Saifuddin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno leaves PH out of 2026 general assembly guest list
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno has not invited Pakatan Harapan to its 2026 general assembly, which will be held from Sept 9 to 12.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Pas was invited in return for the party's invitation to Umno's 72nd Muktamar in Kota Baru, Kelantan.
"If they invite us, we invite them. It is only fair," he told Utusan Malaysia.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier said the decision to invite Pas' top leadership was agreed upon at a party supreme council meeting.
Meanwhile, Zahid said the assembly would not decide on cooperation with any coalition ahead of the 16th General Election.
Instead, he said discussions would focus on the potential benefits and repercussions for Umno and Barisan Nasional should such cooperation be pursued.
"People want to see Malay unity, not only within Umno but also among Malay-based parties.
"I do not want to link this solely to Malay political parties. The Malay community as a whole wants unity to be realised by everyone," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran warns South Korea against involvement in Hormuz
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's foreign ministry on Monday warned South Korea against military deployment or involvement in US operations in the Strait of Hormuz, saying such a move would have "serious consequences."
On Friday, Seoul said it was considering "contributions" to US security efforts in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, which Teheran has largely controlled since the outbreak of war against the United States on Feb 28.
South Korea said it would consider the move provided that its own military readiness was not compromised, but added that no decision had been made.
On Monday, Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei warned South Korea against succumbing to what he called "US pressure and intimidation."
"Any military deployment or participation in operations by other countries in the Persian Gulf or the Strait of Hormuz can only be regarded as direct support for the party responsible for that aggression and will have serious consequences," he said in a post on X.
Iran and the United States have continued to trade fire in and around the Strait of Hormuz, even after an April ceasefire brought the initial intense bombardment campaign to an end.
Negotiations between the two foes have stalled as they vied for control over Hormuz, which normally carries around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas exports.
Since the war erupted, traffic through the vital waterway has been virtually paralysed, disrupting global energy markets.
Iran has required vessels to seek permission to transit – a move opposed by Washington and several regional countries – insisting that there will be no return to the pre-war system of unrestricted navigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt extends RM16bil financing to support MSMEs: Amir Hamzah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has provided RM16 billion in financing facilities so far this year to support the growth and development of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said MSMEs remained a critical component of the Malaysian economy, accounting for about 90 per cent of companies and almost half of employment.
"From the total financing, RM6 billion would be channelled through microfinancing programmes involving agencies including Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia, Tekun Nasional, Bank Simpanan Nasional, Bank Rakyat and Agrobank.
"The remaining RM10 billion would be provided through the Credit Guarantee Corporation and the Small Debt Resolution Scheme via government-backed financing facilities," Amir Hamzah told the media during a visit to Media Prima Bhd's Balai Berita here today.
He was received by Media Prima group chairman Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hussian Aljunid, Media Prima group managing director Datuk Mohd Rafiq Razali and Media Prima's TV Networks, Content and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof.
According to Amir Hamzah, the financing support was particularly important for smaller businesses that may not have sufficient track records or financial records to secure conventional bank loans.
He said the government guarantees would allow banks to extend financing to MSME while reducing some of the risks associated with lending to smaller businesses.
"Microfinancing agencies also provided guidance to businesses, including on proper record-keeping and cash-flow management," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three UiTM students in hospital after endurance challenge to be discharged
Article:
MARAN: Three of the eight Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) students hospitalised after experiencing breathing difficulties during the Komander Kesatria Endurance Challenge (KKEC) on Sept 4 are expected to be discharged today.
Nine students were initially taken to hospital after experiencing health issues during the duathlon event at the UiTM Jengka campus here.
One of them, Fadhlan Fakhry Solana Mohd Fellimal, 21,
later died at the intensive care unit (ICU)
of Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (Hoshas) in Temerloh on Sept 5.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said one of the remaining eight students was still receiving treatment at the Hoshas ICU and was recovering.
"The student is conscious and able to communicate. Another student who was treated in the ICU yesterday has been transferred to a normal ward and will be discharged today.
"Of the six students treated at Jengka Hospital, two have also been allowed to return home today, while the remaining patients are still receiving treatment," he said in a statement today.
Wong said the nine students were participating in the endurance event at 9.57pm when they complained of breathing difficulties before being taken to Jengka Hospital for treatment.
Fadhlan was among three students transferred to Hoshas for further treatment, while the other six were treated at Jengka Hospital.
UiTM Jengka hosted the KKEC duathlon, which attracted 521 participants from UiTM campuses nationwide, except Sarawak.
The multi-sport endurance competition comprised an 8km run, a 20km cycling event and a 10km team endurance event known as Mara Lasak
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia warns of health risks to elderly from volcanic ash
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's Health Ministry said some 3.3 million elderly people in areas surrounding Mount Anak Krakatau, including Banten, South Lampung, Jakarta and parts of West Java, face health risks from volcanic ash, highlighting the urgency of mitigation efforts, reported
Antara news agency
.
"The sharp silica particles contained in volcanic ash make it dangerous to the lungs, eyes and skin.
"When mixed with water, the ash can harden like cement, so improper cleaning can actually increase the risks," the ministry's Director of Health Services for Vulnerable Groups, Imran Pambudi, said here on Monday.
Pambudi stressed that exposure to volcanic ash can cause several health problems, including acute respiratory infections, breathing difficulties, and exacerbation of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
It can also increase cardiovascular risks, including the risk of heart attacks and strokes.
According to Pambudi, the effects of volcanic ash can be felt immediately, while smoke from forest and land fires tends to have a longer-term impact on the respiratory and cardiovascular systems.
"The eyes can become sore, watery and easily irritated, while the skin can become itchy and inflamed.
"Elderly people may also experience confusion and reduced concentration following prolonged exposure. Trauma from sudden evacuation and social isolation can add to the psychological burden," he added.
Mount Anak Krakatau has erupted several times over the past two decades, he said.
In 2018, an eruption triggered a tsunami that killed more than 400 people.
Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, has remained at Level III (Alert) since July 2, the second-highest level in Indonesia's four-tier volcano alert system, with a three-kilometre exclusion zone in place around the volcano.
Meanwhile, this month, volcanic ash from the volcano spread to parts of Lampung, Banten, Jakarta and West Java.
According to Pambudi, eruptions pose health risks to the public, particularly elderly people, who are among the most vulnerable groups.
Hence, comprehensive mitigation measures must be carried out, he said.
People need to use masks and protective eyewear, seal any openings in their homes to prevent ash from getting in, and clean the ash properly.
He also reminded families and caregivers of elderly people to ensure medications remain readily available, to monitor any warning signs, and to provide emotional support.
Moreover, healthcare facilities need to provide oxygen concentrators, medications, salves, eyedrops and personnel ready for emergency evacuations, he said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fire in Indonesia's Papua kills 11, including 6 children
Article:
JAYAPURA: A fire in Indonesia's easternmost Papua region razed a market on Monday and killed 11 people, including six children, police said.
The fire was first spotted in the town of Paniai in Central Papua province shortly after midnight, and it quickly spread to several shophouses, local police spokesman Henry J. Manurung said.
"During the inspection, officers found 11 victims who had died with burn injuries. Of the 11 victims, five of them were adults, while the other six were children," Henry said in a statement.
The children were aged between two and nine years old, he added.
The fire, which raged for more than three hours, destroyed at least 40 kiosks and houses, despite the deployment of fire trucks and water cannons.
Authorities were still investigating the cause of the fire.
"The intensity of the blaze and the fact that the houses and stalls were all packed tightly together made the firefighting process take quite a long time," Henry said.
Deadly fires are not uncommon in Indonesia.
In December, 22 people died when a fire tore through a seven-storey office building in Central Jakarta.
Police said a drone battery that exploded on the ground floor was the likely cause.
An explosion at a nickel-processing plant in the country's east in 2023 killed at least 12 people.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lamborghini among 11 luxury vehicles seized in Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A RM1 million Lamborghini Huracan was among 11 luxury vehicles seized in Penang after their owners failed to renew their road tax and insurance.
The vehicles were seized during the Penang Road Transport Department's (RTD) Luxury operation on Sept 3.
RTD said checks found all 11 vehicles had expired motor vehicle licences and no valid insurance coverage.
Other vehicles seized included Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, BMW, Audi and Toyota Alphard models.
"The offences were estimated to have caused the government more than RM20,000 in lost revenue from unpaid road tax.
"The Lamborghini Huracan, valued at more than RM1 million, drew particular attention after checks found its motor vehicle licence had expired since June.
"The annual road tax for high-powered luxury vehicles of this specification could reach RM12,000," it said in a statement on its Facebook page.
Penang RTD said the value or status of a vehicle would not shield its owner from enforcement action.
It said enforcement would be carried out transparently and without compromise against anyone found violating the Road Transport Act 1987.
Penang RTD also urged vehicle owners, particularly those who could afford luxury vehicles, to ensure their road tax and insurance remained valid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two-month-old baby among five injured in Ulu Bernam crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A family of five, including a two-month-old baby, were injured in a two-car crash along the North-South Expressway near Ulu Bernam early yesterday.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the crash, involving a Toyota Camry and a Mazda CX-5, occurred at KM440.5 of the highway towards Kuala Lumpur.
He said the department received an emergency call at 2.58am before eight firefighters from the Rawang Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the scene.
"The 34-year-old male driver of the Toyota Camry suffered serious injuries and was extricated by firefighters.
"Initial checks found that there were three people in the Camry, but two of them were believed to have fled the scene," he said when contacted.
Ashrul said the Mazda was carrying a family of five, a 34-year-old man and a 34-year-old woman, both of whom suffered serious injuries, as well as three children.
The children comprised an eight-year-old girl and a three-year-old boy, who suffered minor injuries, as well as a two-month-old baby girl who was also lightly injured.
He said firefighters worked to extricate the victims before all of them were successfully removed from the vehicles by 4.20am.
Those injured were handed over to medical personnel for treatment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 'Only two more Fridays before state assembly dissolution' - Ab Rauf
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month.
Speaking at the Jelajah Ketua Menteri Sayang Rakyat programme in the Sungai Udang state constituency today, Ab Rauf, who is also the state Barisan Nasional chairman, said the dissolution could come within "two more Fridays".
"Not long now (before the dissolution). I said the other day there were four more Fridays, but now there are only two Fridays left," he said during a breakfast and meet-and-greet session with residents of Kampung Bertam Ulu here.
Also present was state Senior Executive Councillor and Sungai Udang constituency development coordinator Datuk Rais Yasin.
Yesterday, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged Ab Rauf to expedite the announcement on the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly to pave the way for the state election.
He was reported to have said the announcement should not be delayed for too long, as the people, particularly young voters, should be allowed to determine the direction and future of the state.
Ab Rauf, who is also state Umno liaison committee chairman, confirmed discussions had taken place with several party coalitions to form a political understanding for the state election, but said he was evaluating options to ensure maximum advantage for BN.
"Melaka is like a beautiful maiden with many suitors coming to propose. I find it difficult as a father because everyone keeps asking when we can collaborate.
"For the sake of our struggle, I will not make decisions based on friendship. Instead, I will make decisions based on political strategy to defend and rebuild our party, which has been trampled on and insulted in the past," he said.
He gave assurances that the well-being of Melaka residents remains his administration's main priority, adding that the people's needs would form the foundation of every decision.
He said the mandate given by the people was not for comfort, but to serve by going down to the ground, listening to problems, and overcoming challenges alongside them.
"We will rise together. We were given the mandate to serve the people, and I manage the people well. I could easily sit back in luxury, sleep, and wake up at noon without meeting the people. But no, for the sake of the people, I will face the heat and rain to fight for everything for Melaka.
"Soon will be our 'birthday' (polling day), a birthday where we decide who will represent and defend us. Do not think twice; think of only one thing — that we are 'geng biru' (the blue team)," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zambry tells varsities to stay alert over haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Higher education institutions, particularly those in Sabah and Sarawak, have been urged to closely monitor air quality amid worsening haze in the two states.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said universities, polytechnics and community colleges had been instructed to constantly monitor the situation and comply with government directives.
"We have informed higher education institutions, universities, polytechnics and also community colleges to constantly monitor, especially in the areas of Sabah and Sarawak which are more seriously affected.
"However, we are following these developments and receiving directives from the department, and we will ensure that our students' learning process, wherever they are, will be based on the directives issued by the government," he told reporters after the ceremony for the presentation of undergraduate degree tuition sponsorship letters to the best STPM students of the 2025 batch here today.
He said the ministry would follow any closure decisions made at the state level, citing Sarawak as an example, where Universiti Malaysia Sarawak, three polytechnics and several community colleges would be affected by any such measures.
Zambry said classes had not been disrupted so far, as the ministry had adopted a flexible approach for institutions affected by the haze.
"So far, there is no disruption to our learning process because we are using a more flexible approach.
"If students cannot go to the lecture hall, we conduct classes online," he said.
He was commenting on the ongoing haze situation affecting parts of Sabah and Sarawak, where air quality has deteriorated sharply over the past two weeks.
The Air Pollutant Index (API) in Serian, Sarawak, breached the hazardous threshold of 500 last week, prompting Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia to consent to a
declaration of emergency
for the district.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC to grill several people over fertiliser distribution to Kedah padi farmers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is expected to begin questioning several people this week over delays in the distribution of additional compound fertiliser, or Baja 3, to Kedah padi farmers.
This is part of the investigation, which is still at an early stage. Investigators are also expected to obtain documents related to the supply and distribution of Baja 3.
Investigators are scrutinising information submitted by a farmers' group and reviewing information and issues raised by the Malaysian Padi Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (Pesawah), which lodged a complaint with the Kedah MACC on Aug 26.
MACC had previously confirmed that Kedah MACC opened an investigation following Pesawah's complaint over delays in supplying the fertiliser to padi farmers in the state.
The probe concerns the supply of fertiliser by a company appointed by the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry to meet the requirements of approximately 100,000ha of padi-growing areas under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada).
MACC said investigators would examine the matter not only for possible criminal elements but also any weaknesses in governance which could have contributed to the delays.
The latest investigation bears similarities to an earlier MACC probe into the procurement and distribution of fertiliser for padi farmers under a
RM1.8 billion government contract
.
That investigation examined suspected corruption involving the procurement of fertiliser and raw materials from selected companies as well as possible abuse of power in the selection process.
It led to a former National Farmers Association (Nafas) officer being charged with two counts of receiving US$300,000 in bribes from a Singaporean fertiliser supplier as an inducement to help the company secure an appointment as a fertiliser supplier for padi farmers under Nafas.
There is no indication at this stage that the Baja 3 investigation is linked to the earlier probe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No cracks in federal unity govt, says Pakatan minister as Umno closes gap with PAS ahead of assembly
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — PKR today denied speculations of turmoil among federal unity government components following developments in Umno’s ties with PAS.
PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Pakatan Harapan (PH) continues to maintain good relations with BN, despite Umno’s strategic cooperation with PAS.
He said PKR nonetheless keeps a close watch on shifting political dynamics from time to time,
Harian Metro
reported.
“So far, there are no issues, and all Umno ministers still attended last week's Cabinet meeting.
“We discussed national issues seriously, but there was no political chit-chat during the Cabinet meeting.
“We'll see how things unfold, this is a party matter. I can only confirm there is no turmoil in the Cabinet at this point,” Chang was quoted as saying at a press conference after the National Science Challenge Prime Minister's Cup final here.
He was responding to Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s earlier statement that
PH would not be invited to Umno’s assembly this week, as PAS had already been invited.
Zahid said Umno would focus on the pros and cons of cooperation rather than finalising any coalition arrangement ahead of the 16th general election.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier said the decision to invite PAS’ top leadership was agreed upon at the party’s supreme council meeting.

Title: Selangor police say investigation into Sunway Lagoon ride gone wrong to take at least three months as it waits for tech report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The investigation into the August 22 roller coaster incident at Sunway Lagoon that injured 10 visitors could take another three to four months.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said this is because investigators are waiting for technical reports from several agencies before they can wrap up the case.
“We estimate it may take three to four months for us to obtain the findings of the investigation. This is because we need technical reports from several agencies involved,” he told a news conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters in Shah Alam.
He said police were working with the occupational safety and health department (DOSH), Fire and Rescue Department, forensic teams and other agencies on the investigation.
“Police have taken statements from the staff operating the ride, victims and medical officers,” Shazeli said.
The ride accident occurred at about 9pm on August 22 and involved 22 local and foreign visitors aged between 11 and 44, with no deaths reported.
Selangor DOSH previously said a preliminary investigation found the roller coaster had been operating normally before a “sliding failure” about 200m from the disembarkation point triggered its automatic emergency braking system, causing it to stop abruptly.
As of September 2, all visitors treated and placed under observation at hospitals had been discharged.
The roller coaster remains closed pending completion of the investigation.

Title: No seat for Pakatan at annual Umno assembly, but PAS gets red carpet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Umno will not be inviting its federal government partner Pakatan Harapan (PH) to its general assembly, starting this Wednesday to Saturday.
Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PAS was invited instead, as a reciprocal gesture for the invitation to the Islamist party’s 72nd congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, last weekend.
“There's give and take. If they invite us, we invite them,” he was quoted as saying by
Utusan Malaysia
today.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier announced that the decision to invite PAS had been made in a consensus during a supreme council meeting.
Zahid said the Umno assembly this year would not decide on cooperation with any coalition, particularly ahead of the 16th general election.
He said discussions would instead focus on the potential benefits and risks to Umno and Barisan Nasional should any such cooperation be formed.
“Society wants Malays to champion Malay unity — not just within Umno, but across Malay parties.
“I don't want to unite Malay parties, but as a whole, Malays want Malay unity to be realised,” he was quoted as saying.

Title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Some villages in Nepal have been so completely devastated by the floods that there is no sign they ever existed, according to Malaysian relief volunteers who have seen the destruction first-hand.
Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur.
“The damage is very severe. In some villages, there isn’t even one house left. If someone went there for the first time, they would think there was no village there,” he told
Harian Metro
today.
“In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. In some places, there is no trace of any houses at all.”
Even concrete buildings were not spared, with only about 20 per cent of such structures still standing in some settlements, he said.
“Most of these concrete buildings were also swept away,” Vivegananthan recounted.
Accumulated sludge lines the Trishuli riverbank after flash floods at Trishuli Bazar in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 5, 2026, as survivors struggle to rebuild homes destroyed by the disaster. — AFP pic
Survivors have since been moved away from the worst-hit areas, with many evacuated to Kathmandu and Nuwakot and housed in schools and halls on higher ground.
Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.
In Nuwakot alone, 19 such shelters have been established, he said.
Based on discussions with local authorities and assessments on the ground, food supplies at the shelters were adequate, but survivors needed other forms of assistance.
Mercy Malaysia’s three-member team will remain in Nepal for about 10 days to assess how best to support those who survived the disaster.
Mercy Malaysia’s Rapid Assessment Team assesses the extent of the flood devastation and health needs in Trishuli Dhunge Bazar, Bidur, as relief efforts continue in Nepal. — Picture from Facebook/MERCY Malaysia
Vivegananthan stressed that the team was not involved in search and rescue operations but was focused on helping survivors rebuild their lives.
“We are not involved in search and rescue. We are here to help those who survived,” he said.
Among the assistance provided are medicines, cooking equipment and toys for children, which are being channelled through Nepali authorities, including the country’s Health Ministry.
“The assistance we provide is aimed at helping them continue their lives as best as possible so they can return to normal,” Vivegananthan said.

Title: Two Fridays to go? Melaka CM Ab Rauf drops biggest hint yet on state assembly dissolution
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 7 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month, paving the way for a state election.
The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said the dissolution would come in “two more Fridays”, suggesting an announcement could be made within the next two weeks, Harian Metro reported.
“Not long now. I said four Fridays the other day, but now there are only two Fridays left,” he was quoted saying during at a community programme in Sungai Udang here.
His remarks came a day after Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged Ab Rauf to speed up the dissolution announcement to allow the people, particularly young voters, to decide the state’s future.

Title: RM10,000 and a detour via Surabaya: Malaysian family stranded in Indonesia scrambles to get home after ash cloud cancels flights
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — A Malaysian family stranded in Jakarta after their flight home was cancelled has been forced to spend about RM10,000 on alternative travel, accommodation and transport to get back to Malaysia.
Wan Nor Ridani, 29, said his family had decided to travel by car to Surabaya before flying to Senai, Johor, as direct flights from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur were sold out,
Berita Harian
reported today.
“We have to think of other alternatives because the airport authorities cannot give any assurance when the situation will return to normal,” he was quoted as saying.
The family had already bought new tickets from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur for tomorrow, but decided not to risk another cancellation as airport operations remained subject to intermittent closures.
Wan Nor Ridani said the airport’s operating suspension had been extended until 6pm today, leaving stranded passengers to make their own arrangements.
“Because of that, we will drive to Surabaya and from there take a flight to Senai. From Senai, we will continue to Kuala Lumpur because all direct flights to Kuala Lumpur are already sold out,” he said.
He said he had to split up from some family members as they were unable to secure flights from Surabaya and were still looking for other options.
The continuing eruption of Anak Krakatau since Friday has spread volcanic ash across the region, disrupting domestic and international flights and forcing several airports to suspend operations.
Wan Nor Ridani said the disruption had also sent hotel demand near the airport soaring, with many properties already full.
“Many people are stranded at the airport. Hotels around the airport are all full. The queues to reschedule flights are also very long. Some have been waiting since morning and only got their turn in the afternoon,” he added.

Title: Appeals court reserves decision on bid to stay committal proceedings against former undang Mubarak, five others
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The Court of Appeal reserved its decision on an application by six individuals, including former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak, to stay the committal proceedings against them pending disposal of their appeal.
A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Amarjeet Singh set September 14 for case management to set the date for decision.
The court also extended the ad interim stay of the committal proceedings granted to the six individuals until a decision is made on their stay application.
A different three-man bench of the Court of Appeal had granted the ad interim stay on July 29 pending today’s hearing on the stay application.
Today, the bench heard full arguments for stay of committal proceedings from counsel Awang Armadajaya Awang Mahmud, who represented the applicants, and lawyer Steven Thiru, who appeared for the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU) and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin.
The six individuals comprising four Undangs and two chieftains have appealed against the decision of the Seremban High Court granting the DKU and Raja Norazli leave to commence committal proceedings against them for allegedly breaching an injunction order. Their appeal is scheduled for case management on Oct 19.
The six applicants are Mubarak, Undang Luak of Jelebu Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Undang Luak of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Undang Luak of Rembau Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri, and Shahbandar Sungai Ujong Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid.
In his submissions, Awang Armadajaya said if the stay is not granted, it would render the applicants’ appeal nugatory.
He said there are important legal issues for determination of the Court of Appeal, including whether the High Court or the Special Court had the jurisdiction to hear the injunction and committal proceedings.
He said if the Court of Appeal decide that only the Special Court had jurisdiction, then the case must be brought before the Special Court for determination and all the proceedings in the High Court would be invalid.
Steven, meanwhile, urged the court to dismiss the stay application and allow the committal proceedings in the High Court to proceed without any delay.
He said established legal principle requires contempt proceedings, once commenced, to be given priority over other proceedings, adding that the applicants should instead seek an urgent hearing of their appeal.
Steven further argued that the applicants have shown disrespect to the court and have interfered with the administration of justice and they should not be granted any relief under Section 44 of the Courts of Judicature Act.
The legal dispute originated on May 5 this year when Mubarak and five others filed an originating summons at the High Court to obtain a copy of the minutes of a special DKU meeting held on April 17. Among the contents of the meeting minutes was a decision to remove Mubarak as Undang Luak of Sungai Ujong.
On June 5 this year, the High Court granted an ad interim injunction to preserve the status quo, maintaining the existing composition of the DKU and Raja Norazli’s position as its secretary, pending the determination of issues relating to jurisdiction and justiciability, or until further order of the court.
However, Raja Norazli claimed that media reports on the same day showed that the plaintiffs, particularly Maarof, had been involved in the purported appointment of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan under Article 11 of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959, despite the injunction order still being in force.
He alleged that the appointment was made in defiance of the court order, prompting the DKU and Raja Norazli to seek leave from the High Court to commence committal proceedings against the six individuals for contempt of court. — Bernama
