Title: Police: Missing hikers said they were in good condition when speaking to family on Tuesday
Article:
GERIK, Sept 7 —Police said the six hikers, who are feared missing on Gunung Trans Gerah in Kelantan, were in good condition when they last contacted their family members on Tuesday (Sept 1), before continuing their journey towards Perak.
District police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said the group last contacted their family at 7.47 am that day.
“The group began their hike on Aug 29 from the Pos Dakoh area in Gua Musang, Kelantan, and were expected to make their way out via Pos Kemar, Perak on Sept 3.
“However, as of Sept 6 (yesterday), their family members had yet to hear from them and subsequently lodged a police report out of concern for their safety,” he said in a statement today.
He said following the report, the police, together with the relevant agencies, had coordinated a search and rescue (SAR) operation to locate the group along the trail on the Perak side.
It was reported earlier that the six individuals comprised Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, and two mountain guides, Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43. — Bernama

Title: Police confirm RM27.5m drug syndicate crippled with main suspect shot dead
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police’s (PDRM) Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) crippled a drug processing syndicate suspected of producing Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) worth a total of RM27.5 million in this district and Kuala Lumpur in Op Thrips yesterday.
Bukit Aman NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said in the raid, the 52-year-old main suspect was shot dead after he acted aggressively by firing shots at the raiding team at a terraced house in this district at about 1.30 pm.
He said the house rented by the suspect had been used as a laboratory to process the drugs since early this year, adding that police seized suspected MDMA comprising 64.49 kilogrammes (kg) of liquid, 5.2kg of drug lumps, 7.9kg of drug pills, 104.8kg of drug powder, as well as various drug-processing equipment.
“We believe the suspect obtained the drugs with the assistance of other syndicate members by bringing in drug-processing precursors from abroad.
“The suspect who was shot dead also had the expertise to process these chemicals into MDMA or ecstasy,” he said at a press conference at the Seremban district police headquarters (IPD) here today.
It was believed that the suspect had extensive experience, as his involvement in drug-related activities had been detected since the 1990s, in addition to having three previous arrest and imprisonment records under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Hussein said the main suspect was also wanted under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, in addition to having a previous criminal record under Section 448 of the Penal Code.
He added that the syndicate’s modus operandi was to use residential areas with low population density as locations for processing and distributing drugs to conceal their activities from the authorities.
Hussein said the drugs were believed to be intended for the local and overseas markets, while police were now actively tracking down several more suspects believed to have fled abroad.
Meanwhile, he said police also conducted two separate raids in Seremban 2 and at a house in Kuchai Lama, Kuala Lumpur, which led to the arrest of a 32-year-old woman and a 35-year-old man.
Both the woman and man tested positive for methamphetamine and THC, respectively, and both had various previous criminal records, including drug-related offences. They were remanded for seven days until Sept 13.
Hussein said police also seized three cars and that the case was being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code and Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
He said the seizure could indirectly curb the distribution of drugs to more than 400,000 users. — Bernama

Title: Missing hiking family in Kelantan mountains never stayed out more than a day, says grandpa — now it’s been four, maybe without food
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The silence from his son’s family has left Wan Zairudin Wan Ismail fearing that something may have gone wrong during their hike through the Kelantan forest.
His son Wan Ahmad Aslam, 39, daughter-in-law Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, grandchildren Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, and their two mountain guides have been missing since failing to emerge from the forest as scheduled last Thursday.
“I am worried that someone may have been injured,” Wan Zairudin, 66, who lives in Shah Alam, Selangor, was quoted by
The New Straits Times
as saying today.
The family was last heard from on September 1, when Siti Zulaiha messaged her mother-in-law to say they were safe and expected to reach Pos Kemar in Perak two days later.
Wan Zairudin is also concerned that the group may be running out of food, as their supplies were expected to last only six or seven days.
The six were reported missing after they failed to return as scheduled and repeated attempts to contact them were unsuccessful.
Wan Zairudin lodged a police report at the Bukit Jelutong police station in Shah Alam two days ago.
The Fire and Rescue Department launched a search and rescue operation today, including a helicopter-assisted search to locate the group and trace the route they were believed to have taken.
“My son is a project manager in Yong Peng, Johor, while my daughter-in-law works in Simpang Renggam. They often go hiking with their two children, and the longest they had ever stayed in the forest beyond their scheduled exit was just one day,” he said.
“This time, however, it is worrying as they have now gone four days without sufficient food.”
Wan Zairudin said he had sent the family to Terminal Bersepadu Selatan in Cheras on Aug 29 to catch a bus to Gua Musang, while their car was left at his home in Shah Alam.
The family was due to return by bus from either Gerik or Kuala Kangsar last Thursday before travelling back to Yong Peng, with the children expected to return to school after the holidays ended yesterday.
Wan Zairudin said his son had chosen the Trans GBB route, which he had never attempted before, as part of his plan to complete several mountain expeditions in Malaysia before taking his family to climb Mount Kinabalu next year.
“I am worried that someone may have been injured, perhaps suffering a sprained ankle and being unable to move. Without outside help, it would be difficult for them to get out of the forest,” he said.
Wan Zairudin said the family knew Trans GBB was among the more challenging hiking routes.
He and his wife planned to travel to Gerik today, where search and rescueoperations room had been set up, to seek the latest updates on their family.

Title: Shahrir Samad and Tommy Thomas discussing possible resolution of civil suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The High Court today adjourned proceedings in the civil suit filed by Tan Sri Shahrir Samad against former Attorney General Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Latheefa Koya, and two others, to facilitate settlement negotiations among the parties.
Judge Gan Techiong ordered the adjournment after Shahrir’s counsel Datuk Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin informed the court that his client and the defendants were discussing a possible resolution of the matter.
“As we have indicated earlier, there have been some positive developments and discussions between the plaintiff and the second to fourth defendants. In that regard, we need to obtain further instructions from our client,” said Firoz Hussein.
“We seek Your Lordship’s leave and permission to discuss the matter, specifically the proposed resolution of the dispute. We also respectfully request that this morning’s proceedings be vacated to enable us to continue those discussions. We will return before Your Lordship on Wednesday (Sept 9),” he added.
Counsel Alan Adrian Gomez, representing Thomas as the first defendant, and senior federal counsel Zureen Elina Mohd Dom, appearing for the three other defendants, confirmed that the parties were engaged in settlement discussions and raised no objection to adjourning today’s proceedings.
Judge Gan then adjourned the proceedings to Sept 9 for the parties to update the court on the status of the proposed settlement.
Shahrir had been scheduled to continue giving his testimony in the matter today.
In December 2023, Shahrir filed the civil suit against Thomas, Latheefa, the MACC, and the Government of Malaysia, alleging malicious prosecution.
The former Johor Bahru Member of Parliament’s claim arises from a RM1 million cheque he had received from former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak for rehabilitation works on the Puri Langkasuka housing project in Larkin, Johor.
Thomas, who served as Attorney General from June 2018 to February 2020, has denied Shahrir’s allegations against him, including abuse of power, describing them as “indefensible.”
He further clarified that he had resigned on Feb 28, 2020, and that Shahrir’s criminal trial commenced only on July 26, 2022.
On Jan 5, 2023, High Court Judge Datuk Muhammad Jamil Hussin acquitted Shahrir of the charge of failing to declare to the Inland Revenue Board the RM1 million in income received from Najib. — Bernama

Title: Hadi ready to face police over US ‘topple govt’ claim, says aide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang is expected to give a statement to police after Bukit Aman contacted him over his claim that the United States sought to help topple the Malaysian government before the 2018 general election.
Hadi’s political secretary Syahir Sulaiman said the PAS president was ready to cooperate, although no date has been fixed for his statement, Berita Harian reported today.
“Yes, Bukit Aman has contacted us. Hadi has been informed and is ready to give the police his full cooperation,” Syahir was quoted as saying.
Three police reports have been lodged over Hadi’s claim that the US offered assistance to topple the government in 2014.
He made the allegation at the 72nd PAS congress in Kelantan, claiming several PAS leaders had been invited to meet US Embassy representatives during then-president Barack Obama’s visit to Malaysia that year.
The US Embassy in Kuala Lumpur has denied the allegation, saying its representatives had never offered to help PAS oust the then-Barisan Nasional government.
Chargé d’affaires ad interim David H. Gamble Jr said the United States had never sought to determine Malaysia’s political leadership.

Title: No new wage target, but economy minister says govt wants greater transparency in salary offers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Economy Ministry is looking at ways to make salary offers more transparent and equitable, rather than setting an absolute wage target.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said wage growth was important to ensure the benefits of economic growth were felt by the people.
“Median wages are around RM3,600, but there is still a gap, particularly among the Bumiputera,” he told reporters after a dialogue session at the Royale Chulan hotel here.
Akmal said greater transparency was needed in salary offers to ensure workers received fairer returns for their contributions.
“We need greater transparency in wages, and there should be a mandate for salary offers to be made more transparent and fair,” he said, adding that he would bring the matter back to the Economy Ministry for further consideration.
He said equal opportunities for workers could also be reassessed to ensure young people and other workers had better opportunities and received wages commensurate with their contributions.
Akmal stressed that the approach was not about setting a single absolute salary figure, but about ensuring greater openness and fairness in the wages being offered.
He said wages should, as far as possible, meet people’s expenditure needs, with the Perceived Adequacy of Household Expenditure indicator taking into account factors such as location and household size.
“In the context of wages, what we are looking at is greater transparency in salary offers, rather than setting an absolute figure,” he said.

Title: Four days overdue, rescuers mount land, air and water search for six hikers in Kelantan mountains
Article:
GERIK, Sept 7 — Rescue teams are being mobilised by water, land and air in preparation for a search and rescue (SAR) operation for six individuals feared missing while hiking at Gunung Trans Gerah in Lojing, Kelantan.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (better known by its Malay initials JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received information about the missing two mountain guides and four family members yesterday afternoon, prompting discussions with the JBPM
headquarters’ operations division on the search plan.
He said three boats from the Trojan Jetty in Gerik would transport eight members of the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Team and five fire and rescue mountain guides by water to Pos Kemar.
“A total of 12 Forestry Mountain Guides are also travelling from Sungai Siput in four-wheel-drive vehicles to Pos Kemar, with the journey expected to take about four hours.
“All teams will gather at Pos Kemar, which will serve as the Forward Control Post,” he said when contacted today.
Sayani said the JBPM air unit from the Northern Region JBPM Bertam Air Base was scheduled to depart Bertam at 2pm today for an aerial survey, beginning at the last location where the six were seen on Sept 1 before proceeding towards Pos Kemar.
“The aerial survey is important to give us an initial overview of the search area, including identifying routes that can be used by the ground teams,” he said.
He said the JBPM canine unit which arrived this morning, was on standby but had yet to be deployed pending finalisation of the operation plan.
“A multi-agency coordination meeting is still being held at the Gerik District Police Headquarters to determine the SAR plan and deployment on the ground,” he said.
The operation involves the Royal Malaysia Police, Forestry Department, Department of Wildlife and National Parks, General Operations Force, JBPM and Forestry Mountain Guides.
The six began their hike on Aug 29 and were due to emerge from the forest on Sept 3.
A report was lodged by their family members yesterday after they failed to return as scheduled. — Bernama

Title: Ex-Felda general manager under five-day remand as MACC digs into KL land deal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — A former Felda general manager has been remanded for five days to assist investigations into an abuse of power case involving the appointment of a developer for a project in Kuala Lumpur and the sale of land owned by the statutory body.
The remand order, which runs from today until Sept 11, was issued by Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court here.
The suspect, who is in his late 60s, was among two men in their 50s and 60s called by MACC to assist in the investigation.
Both are suspected of being involved in the sale of the statutory body’s land to a company with interests in the developer, without the knowledge of its board of directors and subsidiary.
It was reported that MACC detained two individuals, including a former general manager of a statutory body with the title ‘Datuk’, at about 4pm yesterday after they appeared at the MACC headquarters here to have their statements recorded.
Yesterday, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.
Last week, MACC opened seven investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).
Abd Halim was reported as saying that the large-scale special investigation, ‘Ops Fella’, focuses on investment transactions and asset acquisitions by Felda and FIC management between 2010 and 2020.
Six of the seven investigation papers were opened on Aug 24, while the remaining one is an old case that is still active and undergoing the Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) process.
The investigations cover the investment in Syarikat Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd, based in Limbang, Sarawak, the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah and the purchase of Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments in London.
They also cover the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd, the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House, and alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.
The old investigation involving the Park City Grand Plaza property, which is still active and undergoing the MLA process, is also being reviewed in parallel, bringing the total number of cases under the seven investigation papers.
Meanwhile, a source said a remand application for the other individual, who is currently receiving treatment for what is believed to be health problems, would be made at a hospital today. — Bernama

Title: Anthony Loke: Steps taken to strengthen checks on aviation personnel including pilots and cabin crew
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) are taking steps to strengthen checks on pilots, cabin crew and other aviation personnel following the case involving a Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilot linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said that was the least they could do now, as the MOT was not privy to details of the police investigation, including the identities of suspects or any arrests made, as the matter was being investigated as a criminal case.
“I’m still not privy to the details…We have read that several arrests have been made, so it is better for the police to be the one making further announcements on the matter,” he said when asked at a press conference held in conjunction with the 61st Directors General of Civil Aviation Conference for the Asia-Pacific Region (DGCA/61) here today.
Loke said MOT would definitely provide full cooperation to police, including access to airport facilities and any information or personnel required for the investigation.
“The investigation is under the police. They have no obligation to inform us or to discuss with us the progress of the investigation, but we will give our cooperation by providing whatever information or access is needed, whether to our facilities or airports, as well as any personnel they want to interview or investigate,” he said.
Last Sept 4, Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police have arrested six local men suspected of involvement in an international drug trafficking syndicate linked to the arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta last July.
The arrests followed information obtained from the 39-year-old co-pilot during questioning by an NCID team sent to Jakarta from Aug 11 to 15.
Media reports previously stated that the co-pilot was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes of drugs and that the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) reportedly seized 15 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills and methamphetamine, with an estimated value of RM45 million.
Meanwhile, on flight diversions following the volcanic ash in Jakarta, CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said Malaysia was assisting by serving as an alternate airport for flights originally bound for Jakarta.
“For Malaysia, we assist them as an alternate airport. So, some aircraft inbound to Jakarta are being diverted to KLIA, so we are supporting them in that respect,” he said.  — Bernama

Title: Two women remanded over alleged child mistreatment at Pahang nurseries
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 7 — Two women have been remanded for six days to assist in investigations into the alleged mistreatment of children at childcare centres in Kuantan and Temerloh.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the two nursery staff, aged 31 and 26, were remanded for six days until Saturday (Sept 12) following applications by police at the Kuantan and Temerloh Magistrates’ Courts.
He said the 31-year-old woman was detained yesterday to assist in investigations into the alleged mistreatment of a two-year-old boy at a nursery in Bukit Setongkol here.
“Another woman was detained to facilitate investigations into allegations of mistreatment involving a two-year-old girl at a nursery in Temerloh,” he said in a statement today.
Kuantan district police chief ACP Ashari Abu Samah said yesterday that police received a report concerning a viral video showing a toddler being scolded, having his hair pulled and his head shaken by a woman working at the centre.
Meanwhile, Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received a report from the child’s 29-year-old mother at about 6 pm yesterday over allegations that her two-year-old daughter had been mistreated by a nanny at a nursery near Temerloh.
The video showing the alleged mistreatment of the child by the nursery caretaker has also gone viral on social media, drawing widespread public attention. — Bernama

Title: Communications minister: Nadi-PKD synergy to optimise government resources, boost public service delivery
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Sept 7 — Efforts to strengthen collaboration between the National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) and Rural Community Centres (PKD) under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) reflect the government’s focus on synergy, resource optimisation and better public service delivery.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Nadi had evolved beyond providing computers and Internet access to become community information and empowerment hubs connecting people with skills, opportunities and government services.
“There are 191 PKDs under KKDW, equipped with facilities, resources and community networks. Given the strengths of both PKD and Nadi, I believe there is significant scope for them to complement each other and strengthen service delivery to the people.
“This is the whole-of-government approach we need to put into practice. It is not about who owns a facility, but how existing government facilities and resources can be fully utilised for the benefit of the people,” he said at the PKD-NADI Strategic Collaboration Workshop here today.
Also present were Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.
Fahmi said the approach was in line with the government’s efforts to promote a cashless society, including the use of e-wallets, while digital empowerment should now be expanded to include artificial intelligence (AI) skills.
“Our hope is for each Nadi to produce at least one prompt engineer. If we prepare young people for the future by teaching them to harness cloud technology and AI, they can develop applications that benefit their communities and local economies,” he said.
In a separate development, Fahmi said he had instructed MCMC to take firm action against the misuse of e-commerce platforms or online marketplaces to sell drugs, including fentanyl.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also contacted him about the issue, which was becoming increasingly concerning.
“I have instructed MCMC, and they will be meeting one of the platforms that we believe has been involved in the misuse of networks enabling drugs such as fentanyl, or what is known as ‘piu-piu’, to be sold in Malaysia,” he said.
Fahmi said government efforts to provide reliable Internet access and improve PKD and Nadi facilities were aimed at narrowing the digital divide between rural, suburban and urban communities.
“But if these communications networks are not secure and users lack the knowledge or skills to protect themselves, it will not only enable drugs to be sold more widely, but also give rise to other problems, including scams,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Inquest told father never consulted over Zara’s autopsy
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 7 — The Coroner’s Court heard today that the father of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir was never asked for his consent regarding an autopsy on his daughter.
Testifying before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan, Mahathir Mohd Hashim @ Marikin, 45, said a doctor confirmed Zara's death in his presence at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I (HQE I) on July 17, 2025.
The 80th witness stated he stayed overnight at the hospital after arriving at the emergency unit on the afternoon of July 16 upon learning of her admission.
Mahathir told the court that a attending female doctor informed him Zara was in critical condition with a broken leg and severe internal bleeding in her brain, lungs, and kidneys, adding that she would remain permanently comatose if she survived.
He further testified that he observed blood on his daughter's pillow, felt an apparent depression at the soft upper back of her neck when kissing her forehead, and noted her left leg was bandaged from thigh to sole. — Daily Express

Title: More than 1,000 homes from RM170,000 set to reshape Perak’s housing landscape in Meru
Article:
IPOH, Sept 7 — More than 1,000 homes priced from RM170,000 are coming to Meru, Perak in a development that could give fresh momentum to the growing township on the outskirts of Ipoh.
Maju Teluk Batik Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Setia Awan Group, has launched the 1,084-unit Residensi Jati De Meru Phase 1B, with the freehold project expected to be completed by 2029 and handed over by 2030,
The Star
reported today.
“We believe home ownership should be within reach of more Malaysians, especially young families and first-time buyers.
“That is why we chose to focus on affordable housing, not just to provide a property, but to create a comfortable and practical home where families can build their futures,” Setia Awan Group director Doh Fan Kent was quoted as saying.
He said the project in Meru Raya, with an estimated gross development value of RM291 million  is aimed at young families and first-time buyers looking for more affordable homes while remaining close to Ipoh.
The development is located near the North-South Expressway, with schools, hospitals, hypermarkets and other amenities within easy reach.
“It is also an area that continues to attract families looking for a more affordable alternative while still wanting the convenience of living within Ipoh,” Doh added.
The project comprises four layouts, ranging from one-bedroom units to four-bedroom units, with prices from RM170,000 to RM358,000.
Setia Awan Group general manager Tan Chong Seng said affordability was a key consideration in planning the development, including efforts to keep facility and maintenance costs manageable.
The development will include a multipurpose hall, children’s playground, kindergarten space and surau.
The developer also plans to build a splash pool outside the residential development that will be open to the public, with residents offered a special entry rate.
The project is currently about 30 per cent complete.

Title: Transport minister: Compulsory carbon tax on aviation centre still in discussion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Malaysia has yet to decide whether to implement a compulsory carbon tax for the aviation sector, although the country remains committed to the International Civil Aviation Organisation’s (ICAO) goal of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
He said Malaysia would adopt a phased approach in implementing measures to reduce aviation emissions, with details to be announced from time to time.
“But in terms of our strategy and implementation, it differs from country to country. As far as Malaysia is concerned, we have yet to determine whether to implement a carbon tax.
“Of course, implementation will take place in stages, an d a more more detailed implementation will be announced from time to time. But at this point, we have yet to make any decision. CAAM (Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia) has not made any decision regarding compulsory carbon taxation,” he told a press conference in conjunction with the 61st Directors General of Civil Aviation Conference for the Asia-Pacific Region (DGCA/61) here today.
Loke said reducing emissions was part of Malaysia’s national obligation as well as an international obligation under ICAO, with all member states requiring to work towards the 2050 net-zero target.
Meanwhile, the conference, hosted by Malaysia for the first time, brings together civil aviation leaders from across the Asia-Pacific region to discuss issues including aviation safety, emerging technologies and sustainability.
Loke said the conference, themed “Smart Skies: Emerging Technologies for Safe, Secure, Sustainable, and Efficient Aviation”, was significant as aviation demand continued to grow while new technologies developed rapidly.
“Technology is already transforming the way aircraft are operated, airspace is managed, and aviation risks are identified. AI (artificial intelligence), unmanned aircraft systems, and advanced air mobility will create further possibilities for connectivity, logistics, and public services,” he said.
He said innovation must be supported by clear policies, credible regulations and strong public confidence to ensure that technological advancement would enhance aviation safety and efficiency rather than create new risks.
Earlier, in his opening remarks, Loke said aviation remained a strategic pillar of national development for Malaysia as an open and trading nation.
“Malaysia aims to strengthen its position as a resilient and competitive regional aviation hub through modern infrastructure, more efficient airspace, strong regulatory institutions and a highly skilled workforce.”
He said Malaysia had established a pathway towards net-zero carbon emissions for international aviation by 2050 through the Malaysia Aviation Decarbonisation Blueprint, aligned with ICAO’s Long-Term Aspirational Goal. — Bernama

Title: Education minister: Parents have discretion in having kids stay home from school if haze worsens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Parents may choose not to send their children to school if they are concerned about their health amid the haze currently affecting the country, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said parents only needed to inform the school if they decided to keep their children at home.
"I understand parents’ concerns over the current haze situation. We hear those concerns. The health and safety of our children remain the priority in every action we take,” she said in a Facebook post today.
She said the ministry would continue to monitor Air Pollutant Index (API) readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE), as well as the latest situation, particularly in affected areas.
Fadhlina said any measures taken would be based on the National Haze Action Plan.
"When the API reading exceeds 100, all outdoor activities are suspended. When it exceeds 200, schools are closed,” she said.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal this morning, Samarahan, Sarawak was the only area to record a very unhealthy reading, at 226.
Meanwhile, 40 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy readings and 24 recorded moderate readings. — Bernama

Title: KLIA becomes fallback for some Jakarta flights after Anak Krakatau eruption
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Malaysia’s main international gateway in Sepang has become an alternative airport for Jakarta-bound flights after volcanic ash from the eruption of Anak Krakatau disrupted air traffic in Indonesia, news outlet
Free Malaysia Today
reported.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Norazman Mahmud said two flights bound for Jakarta had so far been diverted to the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) so far, with Malaysia allowing the airport to serve as a contingency gateway for affected flights.
“Some aircraft bound for Jakarta have been diverted to KLIA. So far, we have received two diverted flights,” he was quoted as saying on the sidelines of the 61st Conference of Directors-General of Civil Aviation for the Asia and Pacific Region here today.
He said one flight from Oman was diverted to KLIA this morning, while another from Saudi Arabia was diverted yesterday.
Indonesia suspended operations at eight airports, including Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau spread across parts of Java and Sumatra from Friday.
About 170,000 passengers have been affected by flight cancellations so far.

Title: Johor to shut schools statewide if API hits 200, as four districts already above 100
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Sept 7 — Johor will close all schools, kindergartens and childcare centres if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 200 amid worsening haze.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali today said several districts were already recording unhealthy readings this morning, with Segamat and Batu Pahat at 157, Tangkak at 153 and Kluang at 151.
“So, if the API reading exceeds 200, the school or learning centre will be closed,” he told reporters during a working visit to SMK Suria Jaya in Parit Yaani here.
Dr Muhammad Naqib said schools were also monitoring outdoor activities during the current hot spell and haze, with the education department empowered to reduce such activities where necessary.
“In light of the current situation, we need to take this matter seriously,” he said.
“If there is an urgent need to reduce outdoor activities, then we will implement it.”
He said the state Education Department is ready to implement the closure under existing standard operating procedures, while district education offices and schools had been told to keep parents, students and teachers updated on API readings.

Title: PMO: King approves end of emergency declaration in Serian
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today consented to lift the emergency declaration in the entire Serian division, Sarawak, imposed last Friday following the haze situation.
The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said the decision was made after taking into account the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and relevant agencies, which found that Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the area were no longer at hazardous levels.
“However, the haze in Sarawak has yet to fully subside, with several areas, particularly Serian and Samarahan, still recording very unhealthy levels.
“The Federal and Sarawak state governments will continue to monitor the situation closely, while residents in affected areas are advised to limit outdoor activities and comply with the authorities’ instructions,” the PMO said in a statement today.
As of 8am today, Samarahan was the only area in Sarawak recording a very unhealthy API reading, at 226.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 40 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy levels, 24 moderate readings and two good levels. — Bernama

Title: National farmers’ group cleans house, shuts nine subsidiaries as scrutiny grows over Malaysian farm support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — As Malaysia’s paddy farmers grapple with delays in subsidised fertiliser supplies, one of the country’s key agricultural organisations is undergoing a major overhaul after years of financial losses.
Pertubuhan Peladang Kebangsaan (Nafas) – the national farmers’ organisation that supports agricultural cooperatives and distributes farm inputs – is shutting nine of its 16 subsidiaries and refocusing on agricultural inputs, its core business which accounts for more than 95 per cent of its revenue.
The restructuring comes as the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission investigates delays in the distribution of supplementary compound fertiliser affecting about 38,000 paddy farmers in Kedah’s Muda Agricultural Development Authority area.
Nafas itself is not implicated in that investigation, but its renewed focus on agricultural inputs puts the organisation at the centre of a business that is critical to farmers and heavily dependent on government support.
Nafas general manager Muhammad Faris Arriffin told
Berita Harian
that the organisation’s restructuring was driven by the financial position it inherited when its current management took over in March 2023.
“When we took over the leadership of Nafas in March 2023, Nafas recorded net losses and had debts of more than RM400 million in the 2022 financial year,” he was quoted as saying.
Nafas general manager Muhammad Faris Ariffin disclosed that the national farmers’ organisation is shutting nine of its 16 subsidiaries and refocusing on agricultural inputs as part of its restructuring drive. — Bernama pic
The turnaround strategy involves closing nine subsidiaries involved in non-core businesses and concentrating resources on areas that can deliver greater value to farmer members and the government.
Nafas’s agricultural-input business includes the distribution of fertiliser and other farm supplies, with government fertiliser contracts worth up to RM2 billion a year.
The organisation’s six remaining subsidiaries are focused on its core businesses, with four involved in fertiliser, pesticides and other agricultural inputs, while two are in the palm oil industry.

Title: Four helicopter passes, 30km downstream – still no sign of Malaysians missing in flood-hit Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — A helicopter search for 17 Malaysians who have been missing nearly two weeks since flash floods hit Nepal’s Rasuwa district has found no trace of the group, their belongings or the six vehicles they were travelling in.
Fishtail Tours & Travels representative Roshan Panday said the helicopter made four passes over the area where the vehicles were swept away but found nothing,
The New Straits Times
reported today.
“It seems the current was at maximum power when it reached that particular spot,” he told the newspaper.
Roshan said several houses had stood near the site, but the force of the floodwaters had left no visible remains of the buildings.
The search team also checked a nearby forest, although it appeared unlikely that the group had managed to reach the area, he said.
The helicopter then flew at low altitude along a 30km stretch downstream from the site but found nothing believed to belong to the missing group.
Meanwhile, the agency split its office team into three groups to search hospitals for any injured members of the group, but none had been found.
The team also checked bodies recovered from the disaster, but none had so far been positively identified as members of the group.
“Search is still on,” Roshan was quoted as saying.
People help a vehicle navigate a damaged, muddy road leading to remote Rasuwa after flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 4, 2026.  — AFP pic
The group was travelling in six vehicles carrying 27 tourists, including 17 Malaysians, two Americans and a Briton.
They were accompanied by seven Nepali crew members, including a doctor who volunteered to provide medical support to the 20 tourists travelling to high altitude.
Six drivers were also part of the convoy, bringing the total number of people involved to 33.
The 17 Malaysians have remained uncontactable since flash floods struck Rasuwa – among the worst hit areas – with search efforts continuing to locate them.
Roshan said on September 1 that the agency would deploy a private helicopter to search for the missing Malaysians.

Title: Malaysian newlyweds’ Bali high turns into five-day airport nightmare, no thanks to Anak Krakatau ash cloud
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 7 — What was meant to be a week-long honeymoon in Bali turned into an unexpected ordeal for a young Malaysian couple after volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau disrupted their journey home, leaving them stranded in Indonesia for five extra days with limited funds.
Amir Hamzah, 29, a factory worker from Kedah, and his wife, Fatin Zulaikha Azizal, also 29, who works for a private company, flew from Bali’s I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport at 8.40pm on Saturday to Jakarta for their 8.30am connecting flight to Kuala Lumpur the next morning.
Amir and his wife were due to return to Malaysia on Sunday but found themselves stuck at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after their connecting flight to Kuala Lumpur was repeatedly delayed and eventually cancelled.
“We thought we would just sleep at the airport for a few hours and then take the morning flight home. We never thought we would end up being stuck here for days,” Amir, who was travelling overseas for the first time, told Bernama.
They had already cleared immigration when the departure information screen showed their flight was delayed, with the departure time pushed back several times before it was eventually cancelled.
The disruption came as volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau forced Indonesian authorities to temporarily close Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and seven other airports, affecting about 150,000 passengers and 467 flights as of Sunday night.
After spending almost 24 hours at Soekarno-Hatta, the couple were informed by Garuda Indonesia that the earliest available flight was on Friday, Sept 11 — five days after their scheduled return.
“When I saw Friday, I was like, ‘Friday? What are we going to do here for another five days?’ We only prepared enough money for our honeymoon and to go home on Sunday,” he said.
He said buying replacement tickets would cost considerably more, while a refund for their cancelled flight would take several days to process.
“We were not told about any compensation, and from what we understood, there would be no compensation because the cancellation was due to force majeure.
“We had just got married, so of course, during the honeymoon we spent a bit more. We initially booked a budget hotel near the airport, but when we started calculating the cost of accommodation and food for another five days, we became worried that the money we had left would not be enough,” he said.
Concerned about how they would manage, Amir contacted Bernama’s Jakarta correspondent for assistance, and the couple were subsequently given temporary accommodation while waiting for help from their family in Malaysia.
Meanwhile, in Malaysia, 31 Jakarta-bound flights scheduled throughout Sunday were cancelled following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta, including 21 at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, according to Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd.
Anak Krakatau, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, began erupting at 11.07pm local time on Friday, with Indonesian authorities reporting volcanic ash reaching about 6,000 metres on the Java side and plumes of up to 15,000 metres towards Sumatra and parts of Banten province. — Bernama

Title: Penang govt auctions Tanjung Pinang land as bypass project races towards 2027 finish
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — The Penang government will auction a 2.42-hectare plot of land in Tanjung Pinang next month to help Consortium Zenith Construction Sdn Bhd (CZC) secure the cash flow needed to complete the remaining works on the Ayer Itam-Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway bypass project.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the state agreed to auction the land after CZC sought assistance to monetise it and obtain the cash flow needed to complete the project by April 2027.
The freehold plot is located at P.T. 858 (Plot 7A), Seksyen 2, Bandar Tanjung Pinang in the northeast district of the island.
“The bypass project is funded not through cash payments to the contractor, but through a land-swap method, where land plots are transferred based on completed work claims,” Zairil said in a statement today.
He said CZC had so far claimed land worth RM695.977 million for completed works.
Of that amount, 4.7ha (11.6183 acres) of land worth RM427.657 million had been transferred to the company, he said.
“Therefore, RM225.768 million in claimed land value had yet to be transferred,” he said.
The project, which links Ayer Itam to the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway, was about 92.46 per cent complete as of August 31, while its financial progress stood at 81.69 per cent, he said.
Zairil said the land, located beside Gurney Bay and Pulau Andaman, has a reserve price of RM313.632 million, or RM1,200 per square foot.
“It will be auctioned at 11am on October 7 at Level 51, Komtar,” he said.
“Profits from the sale will be shared between the state government and CZC,” he added.
Interested bidders must submit a bank draft deposit of RM3,136,320, or one per cent of the reserve price, payable to the District Land Administrator before 11am on the auction day.
Further information is available from the appointed auction agent, One Asia Property Consultants (PG) Sdn Bhd at 25-F Gottlieb Road, 10350 Pulau Pinang, or by calling +604-227 7222.
Participation in the auction is fully subject to the terms and conditions set out in the Proclamation of Sale issued by the Penang state authority.

Title: Stranded by volcanic ash, Malaysians in Jakarta find free beds and open arms
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 7 — When Anak Krakatau’s ash grounded flights across the region, seven stranded Malaysians found themselves with nowhere to go and dwindling patience.
A stranger’s spare bedroom changed that.
Maira Safiraa, an Indonesian who currently lives in Malaysia, opened up her Jakarta house to the group after watching the flight chaos unfold from afar.
“I thought to myself, what if I or my family were in the same situation in a foreign country?” she said in a post on Threads.
That question was enough for her to offer up her home, located about 30 minutes from the airport,
Three of her four bedrooms filled up quickly, and she says the last one is still open, with priority given to women travelling alone.
There is no catch and no bill waiting at the end of the stay.
“The accommodation is free... I am not asking for any payment,” she said.
Anak Krakatau has been erupting continuously since Friday, blanketing the region in ash and forcing six airports to shut their runways.
The fallout has rippled well beyond Indonesia, disrupting flights to Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, Hong Kong, Sydney, Seoul, Doha and Amsterdam.
Maira said the timing worked out — her house happened to be empty apart from her personal assistant, who now has company instead of an empty house to sit in alone.
“I’m actually happy that my home in Jakarta has become livelier with more people around,” she said.
Airport authorities have told her the disruptions are expected to persist until at least 12.30pm tomorrow, longer still if the volcano refuses to settle.
Her goodwill has limits she cannot help — she said she feels for Indonesians stuck in Malaysia in the same predicament, but has no space to return the favour, with her own household already full with her husband, baby and helper.
For now, her open door is one less thing seven Malaysians have to worry about while they wait out the ash.
